shots.caption: My boy Bertram fulls wool. Forty years, and he's never once used a machine to do it.
Cheap synthetic fleece out of China for a tenth of the price. Fine.
What actually finished him was the certification. The form's built for synthetic fabric, it doesn't have a box for wool that was never chemically treated, so it can't be marked safe.
So on paper, every hoodie he makes fails a test it was never built for.
I told him: sell it anyway.
A fabric doesn't need a chemical to prove it's safe. It needed one four hundred years before the form did.
You want a guy for your next hoodie? Hop over to soldanyway.com.
